summary.intent: Push the feat/route-basemap branch, open a PR, run the branch locally end-to-end to visually verify the new street basemap feature, and see the live app with real Strava data.
summary.outcome: PR #1 opened and merged into the review flow; feature verified locally via wrangler dev (tiles, BASEMAP=off fallback, dark/light themes) and then deployed to production, revealing a real timezone bug where recent rides were mislabeled 'today' instead of 'yesterday'; the bug was root-caused, fixed with a new calendarDaysBetween helper, covered by 16 new tests, verified against the real production snapshot, and committed locally (not yet pushed/deployed).

repo: Snapshots written before the basemap change have no `basemap` field and the renderer falls back to the bare 1000x1000 abstract path frame.
`facts.daysSinceLast` is elapsed time (fractional days), not calendar days — never use it for 'today'/'yesterday' prose, only for duration thresholds like DORMANT_DAYS/RECENT_DAYS.

The mood engine's reason string ('and it was today/yesterday') is baked into the snapshot at refresh time, so a fix to that wording only shows up after the next refresh — unlike the render-time 'When' row which corrects old snapshots immediately.

wrangler.jsonc holds a PLACEHOLDER_REPLACED_AT_DEPLOY value for the KV namespace id in git; README instructs pasting the real id before deploy, meaning every real deploy requires a manual edit-then-revert dance.

Pinned wrangler 4.107.0 only supports compatibility_date up to 2026-07-08, but wrangler.jsonc specifies 2026-08-14, so `wrangler dev`/deploy needs an explicit --compatibility-date override; this is pre-existing on main, unrelated to the basemap branch.
Production REDIRECT_URI is set to http://localhost:8787/auth/callback, which will break Strava reconnect if the token ever lapses.

Snapshots never store raw/untrimmed coordinates by design (privacy decision), so a deployed snapshot's real polyline can't be reconstructed locally — reproducing real data requires either a real refresh or real credentials.

code.finding: daysSinceLast computed via daysBetween(last.startedAt, nowMs), i.e. pure elapsed-time duration, not calendar-aware.
Old agoLabel(days) treated any days<1 as 'today' and days<2 as 'yesterday', conflating elapsed time with calendar days; now takes (startedAtMs, nowMs, tz) and computes via calendarDaysBetween.
Second instance of the same elapsed-vs-calendar bug in the 'and it was today/yesterday' reason string; fixed via facts.calendarDaysSinceLast with fallback to Math.floor(days) when absent.
Added calendarDaysBetween(fromMs, toMs, tz): rounds difference of startOfDayMs in tz, so DST 23/25-hour days still count as exactly one day.

Facts interface extended with calendarDaysSinceLast (whole calendar days in athlete tz) alongside existing daysSinceLast (elapsed, fractional) — kept as two separate fields deliberately since thresholds need duration and prose needs calendar.

workflow: For local verification of a Worker-based app with KV storage, seed local KV via `wrangler kv key put --local`, run `wrangler dev`, and curl/headless-Chrome screenshot the result rather than trusting only the test suite.

When a deploy requires a secret/id not committed to git (e.g. real KV namespace id), swap it in temporarily via sed, deploy, then restore the placeholder immediately so the reviewed branch stays unchanged.
Cross-check a suspected timezone bug against real production data (pulled via `wrangler kv key get --remote`) rather than only synthetic fixtures, to confirm root cause before fixing.
When fixing a bug present in two places (render.ts and mood.ts), factor the shared calendar-day logic into one helper (calendarDaysBetween) instead of duplicating the fix.

friction: wrangler dev refused to boot with the committed compatibility_date (2026-08-14) because the pinned wrangler binary (4.107.0) only supports up to 2026-07-08, requiring a manual --compatibility-date override for every local run.
wrangler.jsonc's KV namespace id is a placeholder in git, so deploying real data required temporarily patching the file and reverting it afterward — a repeated manual step.
Local KV was empty, so the first 'run it locally' attempt only showed a synthetic/fake route, causing user confusion until clarified that it was a seeded fixture, not real Strava data.
Two disjoint code paths (render.ts prose and mood.ts reason string) had the same latent timezone bug, requiring a blast-radius check before fixing both.

Existing tests for the 'When' label and mood reasons were written against the elapsed daysSinceLast number directly, requiring rewrites against real timestamps/timezones rather than simple value tweaks.
open_items: Timezone fix (commit 07d5533) is committed locally only — not yet pushed to feat/route-basemap or deployed to production; user was asked whether to push/deploy.
wrangler.jsonc compatibility_date mismatch with pinned wrangler version needs a real fix (bump wrangler or adjust compatibility_date) — flagged as pre-existing and unrelated to this branch.
Decide on a permanent approach for the KV namespace id in wrangler.jsonc (placeholder vs. real value) instead of manually swapping it on every deploy.
Production REDIRECT_URI still points to localhost:8787/auth/callback; should be updated to the real domain before the Strava token lapses.
The mood engine's 'and it was today/yesterday' reason string is baked into snapshots and will only reflect the calendar-day fix after the next refresh/cron run, not immediately on deploy.
